cross_market_insights: All four SERPs open with an AI Overview; organic page one is dominated by Pinterest pins, Instagram and low-authority lifestyle blogs (Nigeria-based publishers). No authoritative planner or tourism page holds the term in AU.

AU results lean to honeymoon intent (fashionpoliceng, Tripadvisor honeymoon resorts); London leans to commercial safari-wedding operators (Instagram planner, Belafrique). Our African honeymoon page owns the honeymoon side; this piece must stay on wedding intent.

Nobody in the top 3 covers, per destination: whether a legal wedding is possible for foreigners, the right months for a wedding (not just a holiday), the official travel advisory, or guest logistics (light aircraft luggage limits, camp capacity, room blocks, transfers).

Local packs and a knowledge panel for South African venues appear in Melbourne and Brisbane: Google reads the term partly as 'South Africa venues'. Cape Town and the Winelands deserve two strong cards.
Content is stale: several top results are 2015 to 2021. A dated, criteria-led 2026 ranking with official sources is a clear freshness gap.
payload.recommended_angle: An editorial ranking of 12 African wedding destinations across safari, coast and islands, North Africa and the Cape Winelands, judged on the same stated criteria (setting, best wedding months, legal or symbolic, exact Smartraveller level, guest travel), showing what a Wedded Advisor handles behind each: camp buyouts and guest numbers, light aircraft transfers, wet season, legal paperwork, room blocks.
